summary: Comprehensive architecture designed for History tab, nutrient enrichment (12 nutrients), meal management (edit/delete/add), dashboard integration, and full module contracts. All acceptance criteria addressed: data layer schema with extended columns, UI component hierarchy with swipe navigation, 5 ADRs documenting key decisions (storage, gestures, overrides, migration, navigation), and module contracts for MealRepository, HistoryViewModel, HistoryRoute. Design preserves existing clean architecture and Jetpack Compose patterns; backward compatible with nullable columns and graceful degradation.

manual_steps: Review architecture.md for data/UI/domain layer structure and component hierarchy
Review ADRs (ADR-001 through ADR-005) for detailed decision rationale and tradeoffs
Verify all 12 nutrient columns named consistently (saturated_fat_100, sugar_100, iron_100, calcium_100, magnesium_100, zinc_100, vitamin_c_100, vitamin_d_100, vitamin_b12_100)
Confirm migration strategy: MIGRATION_2_3 adds nullable columns without data conversion
Validate MealRepository, HistoryViewModel, HistoryRoute contracts match spec requirements
Design database schema diagram (recommend: visualize FoodItemEntity, MealEntryEntity, DailySummaryEntity with new columns)
Design UI wireframe for History card (meals with 12 nutrient display + edit/delete/override buttons)
Confirm Italian strings (strings-it.xml keys) for new UI labels: 'Storico', 'Modifica valori nutrizionali', nutrient names
Plan gesture testing strategy: swipe distance/velocity thresholds on devices with different screen sizes
Determine OFF API integration timeline (not in scope; separate task)
findings: Existing HistoryRoute skeleton and HistoryViewModel foundation already present; design extends minimally
MealLoggingViewModel can be reused for edit/add flows (supports date pre-population)
DailySummaryEntity denormalization fits fast History queries (no query-time computation needed)
Dashboard macronutrient card requires minimal modification (add onClick callback; visual feedback via Material 3)
5 ADRs resolve all major decisions: storage pattern, gesture mechanism, override scope/UI, migration approach, navigation flow
Backward compatibility assured via nullable columns; no breaking changes to existing data or queries
notes: TRADEOFF: Stored meal totals (MealEntryEntity) are immutable once saved; corrections to OFF baseline don't retroactively update old meals. By-design; document clearly.
TRADEOFF: One override per food (not per-meal); simpler mental model but less flexibility. Extensible for per-meal overrides in future via new entity.
TRADEOFF: Nullable columns require null-safety in queries (SUM(COALESCE(...)) pattern); standard Room/Kotlin best practice.
ASSUMPTION: OFF (Open Food Facts) provides or will provide enriched nutrient data (saturated fat, sugar, minerals, vitamins) for foods. If unavailable, fields remain NULL.
ASSUMPTION: Screen reader accessibility tested separately by QA; design includes fallback buttons for swipe navigation.
ASSUMPTION: Gesture velocity thresholds (400 dp/s, 50 dp min distance) chosen conservatively; adjust based on beta feedback.
NEXT: Designer phase will create detailed UI mockups for History card, daily totals section, and override dialog.
NEXT: Planner phase will break architecture into implementation tasks with dependencies (Phase 1-5 suggested priorities in design-summary.md).
NEXT: Coder phase will implement entities, migrations, DAOs, then UI components following Planner task sequence.
